input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: a Content-Type parameter without an equals sign is stored with the value True instead of being skipped
- failure path: the header `text/html; charset` yields params['charset'] == True; get_encoding_from_headers (shown below the change) returns params['charset'].strip(...) which raises AttributeError on a bool, so reading response.text for such a response fails instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1

Reviewer finding
- description: Parameters without '=' are now stored with value True. In get_encoding_from_headers, `params["charset"].strip(...)` is called on that value, and bool has no strip.
- rationale: Trigger: a header like `Content-Type: text/html; charset` (bare charset token with no '='). The parser stores params_dict['charset']=True, then `True.strip("'\"")` raises AttributeError. Previously such params were skipped. Impact: response.encoding / r.text crashes on a malformed but plausible header.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: a parameter with no '=' is stored as True. That bool then reaches .strip in get_encoding_from_headers and raises AttributeError for 'text/html; charset'. Root cause, trigger and failure all match the label.
